tasks.redPrompt:
RED for #253 (rules: _shared of teams/mvox-dev/memory/pipeline-args/args-253.json — read it first). PO ruling governs; five pins, in priority order.

(1) FIRST-CLASS DELIVERABLE, DO IT FIRST — condition the mock. page.roster-indent.spec.ts:693-717 pins the exact 'reparent lands, renumber fails' scenario but its listSectionsMock returns one static fixtureTree() unconditioned on prior writes, so it proves reconcile FIRES, not that reconcile is TRUTHFUL. Recondition listSectionsMock so that after a successful reparentMock call the refetched tree reflects the landed _parent move (and without one, the original tree). Then assert the reconciled DOM shows the section AT ITS NEW PARENT/DEPTH (the truth) — not reverted. PO: 'confirm in the report that the conditioned mock fails against today's code before the fix lands.' Run it against current main and REPORT the failure output — a regression test that passes before the fix is not testing the fix.

(2) Typed SectionReparentPartialError (sectionErrors.ts — currently only SectionMembershipMissingError + SectionNotEmptyError). Follow house precedent: SeriesCascadePartialError's counts (seasons/deleteErrors.ts), ProfileSaveError's createdProfileId (profile/applyProfileSave.ts). Must carry: which step failed ('reparent' | 'renumber'), renumber progress (k of N), captured HTTP status AND response body. Full-shape toEqual assertions on the error object.

(3) Body capture. reorderSections (sectionActions.ts:305-337, throws at :315,330,334) and reparentSection (:451-483, throws at :462,477,481) throw with only res.status — no body read. New tests: mock non-2xx with a body text; assert the typed error carries both status and body, and that the captured body reaches console.error (post-hoc human-readable evidence — PO: 'not only a thrown message that gets swallowed'). Also pin a mid-loop failure in a multi-section (N>1) sibling group — no such test exists (research-confirmed gap).

(4) Two banner states, not three (roster/+page.svelte:2550-2560 today gates one fixed roster_section_reorder_failed on one boolean). Pin: (a) reparent itself failed → nothing landed → EXISTING copy stays; (b) reparent landed, renumber failed → NEW copy that tells the user the section DID move (new i18n key; GREEN adds all 4 locales). The renumber depth k/N goes in the typed error only — assert it is NOT rendered in the banner.

(5) Refusals, pinned as tests: NO retry/backoff (assert exactly one reparent request and no repeated POST/DELETE sequence on failure — retrying this non-idempotent sequence can duplicate property values); NO automatic unwind (assert no reverse _parent write is issued after a renumber failure — the landed move stays, the banner tells the truth).

Do NOT touch: tabindex=-1 pins (spec :828-903), structuralWritePending guard, canIndent/canUnindent, the single listSections refetch + snapshot fallback shape.

tasks.commitBody:
A section indent/unindent is two writes: the _parent move, then a
serial renumber of the destination siblings. When the renumber
failed partway, the shared catch reported 'did not save' — but the
move HAD landed, and the only evidence (the server's response body)
was discarded; only a status number survived.

Three changes, per PO ruling on the root-cause report:

The one existing test for this exact failure could not see it —
its listSections mock returned the same static tree whether or not
the move landed, proving reconcile fires, not that it is truthful.
The mock is now conditioned on prior writes and was confirmed to
fail against the pre-fix code before the fix landed.

Failures now throw a typed SectionReparentPartialError (house
precedent: SeriesCascadePartialError, ProfileSaveError) carrying
which step failed, how far the renumber got, and the captured HTTP
status AND response body — logged where a human can read it after
the fact. Every future occurrence yields evidence; no live probe
needed.

The banner now tells the truth in two states: nothing landed keeps
today's copy; a landed move with failed ordering says the section
DID move, in four locales. Deliberately refused, per ruling: no
retry (the sequence is not idempotent — a retry after an ambiguous
timeout can duplicate values), no automatic unwind (a reverse write
against a system that just failed a write compounds the failure).
The landed move stays; the user can see and redo the ordering.

Live gate (Joosep): none reproducible on demand — the fix pays out
as readable evidence on the next real occurrence.
